hypothesis: Reusing one verified Hyperliquid REST completed-minute candle snapshot per symbol can materially reduce V58 shared-IP request weight without changing completed-bar OHLCV, route decisions, or completed-bar exit decisions.
decision: Continue the authority-none 15-minute cached-observer versus uncached-live parity watcher until the preregistered 1,440-minute window is complete. Do not modify or restart the live backend. After exact OHLCV coverage passes, run route, entry-freshness, opposite-exit, maximum-hold, and completed-bar profit-lock decision parity before presenting a live-cache cutover request. Direct WebSocket substitution remains rejected by the sealed source-parity evidence.
falsifier: Reject or revise the live-cache challenger if the watcher records any internal missing row, conflicting duplicate, or cached-versus-uncached OHLCV mismatch; if any identical completed-bar input changes a V58 route or exit-controller decision; if request reduction is below 70 percent; or if post-change HTTP 429 and cycle-latency behavior does not materially improve.
limitations: The current exact prefix is 220 completed minutes per asset, not the preregistered 1,440-minute window.
DuckDB is a bounded asynchronous import of the live ledger, so newer observer-only tail rows are reported separately from internal gaps.
Live telemetry preserves accepted completed bars but does not serialize every redundant REST response.
Zero OHLCV mismatch does not prove that a very late venue revision can never occur.
Exact candle parity does not yet prove route, entry-freshness, maximum-hold, opposite-exit, or profit-lock decision parity.
Shared-IP aggregate request weight remains inferred rather than centrally measured per endpoint.
No profitability conclusion follows from transport reliability evidence.
